title: Humans probably invented writing from scratch four separate times
body: Most scholars recognize four independent inventions of writing: in Mesopotamia around 3400–3100 BC, in Egypt around 3250 BC, in China before about 1250 BC and in Mesoamerica before about AD 1. Mesopotamian cuneiform grew out of a much older system of clay tokens used for accounting, and China’s earliest surviving texts are inscriptions on oracle bones. Whether Egypt borrowed the idea from Mesopotamia is still debated.

slides.heading: Four separate inventions of writing, years ago
slides.note: Approximate ages; whether Egypt borrowed the idea from Mesopotamia is still debated.

slides.question: What did Mesopotamian cuneiform grow out of?
slides.explanation: Cuneiform grew out of a much older system of clay tokens used for accounting. China’s earliest surviving texts, by contrast, are inscriptions on oracle bones.

slides.heading: Match the region to its earliest writing
slides.explanation: Cuneiform grew out of clay accounting tokens, China’s earliest texts are on oracle bones, and Egypt’s hieroglyphs go back to about 3250 BC.
